chapter: Lucky Roberts, Armstrong and the big-band rivalries
title: Leaving Lucky for jazz; Joe Smith, Doc Cheatham, Cuban Bennett, Jabbo Smith
summary: He left Roberts because jazz mattered most after hearing Armstrong, and praises Joe Smith, Doc Cheatham, Cuban Bennett and Jabbo Smith's battle with Armstrong.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Getting back to what we were talking about, Lucky Roberts, well then I left Lucky Roberts because jazz was my paramount issue. And I'd heard Louis Armstrong, and that was it, then.
Yet, speaking of trumpets, I was influenced also by Joe Smith.

always loved that beauty. MR. BUTLER: Oh, yes, and I. And then Doc Cheatham And there was another boy name of Cuban Bennett. He played that beautiful horn but he had control, and those progressions he was making, they were something else. And they had another fellow around and was playing fast, just as fast as this one, playing as much horn as anyone, his name was Jabbo Smith. And he and Louis Armstrong, told me, had a battle. And one didn't know who was winning, only Louis Armstrong had that particular delivery. And the sound that it had, and the sound had that soul.
And I was trying to get all these in together. That's what was creating -- I was becoming Jack Butler.
